source: make 3d interact able game with rounds. a random players avatar is chosen and every player becomes them, player name tags are removed during rounds. players have to guess who the original player is because everyone looks the same. create soft rustic lobby area with dim lamps and fancy seats you can sit in. rounds will occur in a hotel like building with similar easthetic, everyone will teleport here when round begins. rounds last 3 minutes, during which everyone can select who is the real player, all players who guess correctly gain a point. when times up or everyone has voted round ends. when round ends a collapsable results display is shown before everyone is teleported to lobby. during round everyone Is named a number from 1 up to 10 depending on number of players instead of their name tag.

answers.ask: How big is the hotel - a handful of rooms players can sweep in three minutes, or a large building they can get lost in?
answers.answer: Use a small hotel with a handful of rooms and connected hallways that players can sweep within the three-minute round.

answers.ask: Is the hotel one shared space everyone mills around in, or should it have separate rooms that split the group up while they guess?
answers.answer: Make it one shared hotel space with separate rooms connected by hallways, so players can move around and observe each other without being isolated.

scene_prompt: Create a 3D game map with a soft rustic lobby and a separate small hotel round area. The lobby has dim lamps and elegant sit-down seating arranged as a relaxed waiting space. The hotel shares the same rustic aesthetic and is one connected, shared interior: a handful of rooms linked by hallways, compact enough for players to sweep through within three minutes, with open circulation between rooms so the group can observe one another without isolation.
blob:
### Genre
The dominant genre is Party & Casual: timed rounds in which a group gathers, moves through a shared round space, and returns to a lobby. The round rules establish the genre but do not add layout geometry.

### Shape and preset
Use `space-staged`, matching the Minigame preset. The prompt explicitly separates a waiting lobby from a distinct hotel round map; retain the preset shape but omit its unrequested scoring, spectator, and display features.

### Config requirements
Use `social-hub` as visible geometry: the lobby is an open, relaxed gathering area with seating concentrated around its warm light. No other configuration options are required. The round transition, voting, player labels, and results display are mechanics or UI, not visible layout components.

### Layout components
Build two separate interior zones. The lobby is a compact rustic waiting room, sized for the full group to stand and sit together, with dim table lamps, warm wood finishes, soft upholstered fancy chairs and sofas, and clear open floor circulation. The hotel round area is a separate small, connected rustic hotel interior: a central hall or foyer feeds a handful of distinct rooms through connected hallways. Keep every room visually open to the circulation network through broad doorways or glazed openings where appropriate, so players can circulate, see others passing, and are not isolated in dead-end spaces. Use warm wood flooring, muted wallpaper or plaster walls, rugs, lamps, side tables, and hotel-style doors; do not add exterior grounds. Enclose both zones fully as interiors. Frame the lobby as an inviting, centered social room, while the hotel composition should show the central hall and branching connected rooms in one readable compact plan.

### Render order
Use `topdown` first, authoritative, because the hotel’s room-to-hallway connectivity must remain readable and allow the shared group to sweep the whole area without accidental isolation.

### Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is small, driven by the handful of hotel rooms intended to be swept within a three-minute round. Theme: soft rustic, warmly lit boutique hotel. Use `P4` because the lobby and hotel round area are separate maps, and `P0` otherwise; no stacked surfaces, exterior-to-interior transition, or validity-by-construction geometry is required.
